title: Causality Lens for Timeouts, Overload, and Model Rejections
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a single-pane operational 'causality lens' that helps SREs, runtime engineers, and PMs quickly distinguish why requests fail or timeout across layers (client, router, queue, model compute, and network) and to separate overload vs model-level errors (safety rejects, OOMs, decode errors, or model exceptions).

Scope:
- Instrumentation: extend tracing hooks to attach standardized tags: error_origin (client/router/queue/model), model_variant, model_error_code, grpc_status, http_status, route_id, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, and gpu_util_snapshot.
- Metrics/log pipeline: map error tags to ClickHouse metrics tables and enrich traces in Tempo/Jaeger; index key fields in ES for fast query.
- Dashboards: new 'Causality Lens' dashboard with: global top-line error ratio, stacked error-source breakdown, timeouts sub-classified (client abort / router queue timeout / model compute timeout), overload indicators (avg queue depth, tail batch sizes, GPU util), model rejection reasons, and HTTP/gRPC code mapping.
- Alerts & Runbook: SLO-driven alerts for per-route p99 latency and error-ratio with actionable playbooks that map diagnostics to remediation steps.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce mean MTTR for incidents caused by timeouts/overload from baseline by 30% within 3 months.
- >90% of new incidents have an initial diagnosis tag (error_origin).
- Dashboard panels populate with data for 95% of routes within 48 hours of rollout.

Instrumentation details & tradeoffs:
- Tracing hook changes: add 6 new span tags described above. Hook is implemented in trace-propagation v2 lib (PR linked below). We need to keep tag payload small to limit trace size and sampling costs — use enums for error_origin and model_error_code.
- Sampling policy: adaptive sampling that keeps 100% of traces for requests that hit p99 latency or non-2xx status, and otherwise 1% baseline. For new model variants or routes with rising error ratio, bump sampling to 50% for 24h. This balances cost vs signal for causal analysis.
- Metrics pipeline: use existing metrics exporter to ClickHouse for counters/histograms and send enriched traces to Tempo. Logs with stack traces go to ES with a TTL of 30 days.

Dashboard panels (implementation notes):
1) Top-line tiles: total requests, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, avg queue depth.
2) Error provenance waterfall: stacked time series by error_origin with drilldown to model_error_code and grpc/http codes.
3) Timeouts breakdown: pie/table with counts for client-abort, queue-timeout, compute-timeout, network-timeout; include median latency for each.
4) Overload heatmap: route x minute grid showing queue depth and batch size; correlate with GPU util and scheduling delays.
5) Rejection catalog: table of model_error_code (safety_reject, decode_error, oom, internal_exc) with sample trace links and top prompt fingerprints.
6) RCA helpers: trace sampler controls, quick query links (ClickHouse/ES/Tempo) and playbook buttons (pager, annotate incident).

Alerting & SLOs:
- New alert: route-error-rise: when error-rate increases by >3x baseline and absolute error-rate > 0.5% in a 5m window.
- SLO guard: p99 latency per-route > threshold (configurable) for 10m => notify on-call and create incident.
- Alert actions include automated trace capture with full payload for sampled traces (privacy masking applied).

Rollout plan: canary on dedicated tier routes for 1 week, validate overhead (<3% latency tail increase), verify sampling & storage cost, then expand to hosted API with phased windowed rollout.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Trace retention vs cost: need budget guardrails; propose 30d for full traces, 90d for metrics.
- Privacy: some prompt payloads may be sensitive. We'll add redaction hooks and store only partial prompt fingerprints except for incidents with explicit approval.
- Backfill: historical traces will not have new tags; dashboard should surface 'tag missing' bucket.

Linked artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Causality+Lens+Design
- Trace lib PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-propagation/pull/162
- Spike notes & perf numbers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleSpikeDocs

Next steps (first two sprints):
- Sprint 1: merge trace lib change, implement enum mapping, add metric exporters (ENG-90378).
- Sprint 2: dashboard panels + alert rules, runbook authoring, canary rollout on dedicated routes (ENG-90379).

If the team prefers, scope can be trimmed by starting with model_error_code and timeout subclassification first and deferring adaptive sampling to a follow-up (lower initial cost but slower root-cause resolution).
